es a top-level `reasoningEffort` for a\nper-request effort. Like `temperature`, it is pinned on the session's **first\nturn** (a c

The SDK, CLI, MCP tools and in-app agent all go through the same operations:
`--effort` / `reasoningEffor

## Not in the API yet

To set expectations while in preview, these are **not** available over the API
today (most exist in the

hosted inspector UI):

* Creating or revoking API keys (UI-only by design; see [Authentication](#authentication))
* Chat and co
nformance suites\n* Browser-based OAuth flows initiated by the API (complete OAuth yourself,\n then upload the token to one of th

e server's [accounts](#server-accounts))

If one of these blocks you, tell us on
[Discord](https://discord.gg/JEnDtz8X6z); it d

irectly shapes what we
stabilize first.

## Versioning & stability

* The API is **path-versioned** (`/api/v1`). When it reac
hes general\n availability, breaking changes will require a new version path.\n* **During the preview**, breaking changes to v1 m
ay still happen; we'll note\n them in the [changelog](https://docs.mcpjam.com/changelog/overview.md).\n* **Additive changes** (ne
w endpoints, new optional request fields, new\n response fields, new error codes) are considered non-breaking and can ship\n at

any time. Write clients that ignore unknown fields.
* Error **codes** are stable identifiers; error **messages** are not.

###

Renamed surfaces

Three nouns this API used are now what the product calls them: `scenario` is
**study**, `journey` is **goal**

, and `wave` is **swarm run**. The paths, the
operation names, the SDK types and the noun-bearing response fields all moved:

|

Was | Is |
| - | - |
| `/projects/{projectId}/scenarios[/{scenarioId}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies[/{studyId}]` |
| `/pr
ojects/{projectId}/user-testing/scenarios/{scenarioId}/…` | `/projects/{projectId}/studies/{studyId}/…` |\n| `/projects/{projectId
}/environments/{environmentId}/scenario` | `.../environments/{environmentId}/study` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys[/{journey
Id}]` | `/projects/{projectId}/goals[/{goalId}]` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journey-runs/{runId}` | `/projects/{projectId}/goal-r
uns/{runId}` |\n| `/projects/{projectId}/journeys-overview`, `.../journey-findings` | `.../goals-overview`, `.../goal-findings` |\
n| `/projects/{projectId}/waves/{waveId}/insights` | `/projects/{projectId}/swarm-runs/{swarmRunId}/insights` |\n\nResponse fields
followed their nouns: `scenarioId` → `studyId`, `journeyId` →\n`goalId`, `waveId` → `swarmRunId`, and `sessionsPerTarget` → `iter

ations`.

Two reads became one: `get_scenario` served the execution settings and
`get_user_testing_scenario` served the environ
ment id and the insights\nenvelope. `get_study` returns both, and the two caller-dependent fields are\nabsent rather than null whe

n you may not have them.

**Every old path still works** and is unchanged, including its old response
spellings. Each one answe
rs with `Deprecation: true` and a `Link` header naming\nits successor. The old paths are not in the OpenAPI spec, and they are rem

oved
at general availability.

A handful of operations kept their names through the rename and so have no
deprecated twin to h
old the old field spellings. `get_swarms_overview`,\n`create_swarm` and `update_swarm` emit both and accept either, never both in\

none request, until general availability.

### Vocabulary

Renamed field values cannot be aliased the way paths are, so they a

re chosen
by header. Send `x-mcpjam-api-vocabulary: 2` and the renamed values read
canonically:

| Field | Vocabulary 1 | Voca

bulary 2 |
| - | - | - |
| session `sourceType` | `scenario` | `study` |
| session `parentRef.kind` | `scenario`, `journeyRun`
| `study`, `goalRun` |\n| session `parentRef` ids | `scenarioId`, `journeyRunId`, `journeyRefId` | `studyId`, `goalRunId`, `goalRe

fId` |
| share `resourceType` (field AND path segment) | `scenario` | `study` |

Absent means `1`, which is byte-for-byte today
's contract. Any other value is a\n`400`. On the way IN, a vocabulary-2 request may name a filter or a path segment\nby either spe
lling; a vocabulary-1 request may use only the legacy one. A response that varies by vocabulary sends\n`Vary: x-mcpjam-api-vocabul

ary`.

This is a **separate header** from `x-mcpjam-eval-vocabulary`, which is
eval-scoped by name and moves on its own schedul
e. A deployment may speak one\nand not the other, so read\n`GET /projects/{projectId}/capabilities` (`apiVocabulary` and `vocabula

ry` are
two blocks) before sending either. With the SDK:
`new PlatformApiClient({ …, apiVocabulary: 2 })`, or
`client.withApiVo

cabulary(2)` on one you already hold.

Permalink resource types work differently: `study` and
`goal_run` are the canonical keys
, `user_testing_scenario` and `journey_run`\nstill resolve to the same routes, and which one a response carries follows the\nOPERA
TION rather than the header; a renamed operation derives the canonical\nkey, its deprecated twin the old one. `capabilities.apiVoc

abulary.resourceTypes`
lists both.
